# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - The middle of October was a relatively quiet period for precious metals prices. All of the metals traded in a similar fashion to equities, even gold, with risk on/risk off trades the order of the day. Market sentiment seems to be becoming more positive towards the possibility that European leaders may eventually emerge with a plan to address their debt issues in the nick of time. The current mood in the precious metals markets is therefore cautiously bullish. • The most recent Commitment of Traders Report reports further substantial falls in long speculative interest in gold and silver for the week to the 18th of October, with price declines eroding any residual bullishness. The heavy declines in speculative positioning in platinum and palladium slowed dramatically, indicating that investors may now believe that the selling seen in these metals was rather overdone. • ETF holdings grew for gold and palladium but declined for silver and platinum in the week to the 21st of October. Sentiment was not extreme though, with changes in the amount of each metal held being relatively small. ##### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **24 October 2011** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **24 October 2011** ### **Gold CFTC data to 18 October 2011; ETF data to 21 October 2011.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

*21-Oct-11**|39,465,716|5,279,632|3,694,889|409,748|1,377,374|6,792,696|5,441,041|3,304,292|1,639,139|**67,404,527**| |**Change**|**0**|**16,584**|**9,764**|**0**|**-54,569**|**74,748**|**11,388**|**56,000**|**0**|**113,915**| - Movements in the gold price were rather sedate compared to those of recent weeks following the 11th of October. Gold started by holding the $1,675 level and slowly pressing higher as the Dollar weakened. Interestingly, gold now seemed to align itself with equities in price terms, moving higher on good economic news rather than on risk events. With the price at lower levels than a month earlier, Indian physical buying was strong and this was accompanied by the return of Chinese buying following the National Day holidays. When Slovakia rejected the proposal to expand the EFSF’s remit, the market shrugged and gold moved up to a weekly high of $1,694 on the 17th. Following that, though, news emerged that Chinese GDP was weaker than had been expected. Equities were sold off and gold fell back to $1,630 on the 18th. A slow global economy remained a concern, driving gold down to a low of $1,605 on the 20th. However, confidence started to build that European leaders might yet repair their debt situation. Markets responded positively and gold rebounded to trade close to $1,660 today. - In the gold market, investor interest declined once again, falling by almost 900,000 ounces to 20.8 million ounces. Japanese investors were buyers, adding 83,000 ounces of long positions to take their total positioning to 1.42 million ounces. On COMEX, however, net long speculative positions fell by just under one million ounces to 19.4 million ounces as the price slipped lower. This is a very substantial worsening of bullish sentiment since the start of August when positions stood at 33 million ounces. - Gold ETF holdings increased by 114,000 ounces in the week to the 21st of October, rising to 67.4 million ounces. SPDR holdings were unchanged but the majority of funds which we monitor saw net buying. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—October 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- The gold:silver ratio stayed fairly constant during the middle of October with silver essentially following gold as both behaved like growth assets. As with gold, silver’s range was restricted in price terms. It started the 11th just above $32 and ounce and reached its high for the week, of nearly $33, on the 12th. The price started slipping back slowly, however, falling back to $32 at the start of the following week, partly driven by downgrades of the credit ratings of Spain and a number of European banks. When poor Chinese GDP data was released on the 18th, silver was sold off rapidly, dropping to $30.43 before bouncing back above $32 later that day to confuse the market. Concern emerged that the EU was to fail to meet its own target of October 23rd to reach agreement on solving the Euro crisis. Silver fell back to touch $30 on the 20th before moving higher as the market turned to optimism for no clear reason. Whatever the trigger, silver has since moved higher to trade around $31.60 currently. - A further decline in the silver price drove still more liquidation by futures investors. Net long speculative positions in this metal on COMEX fell by 12 million ounces, reversing the more bullish investor behaviour of the previous we

ek. They now stand at 124.6 million ounces. Long exposure fell in the options market in particular but the number of short positions held by investors increased substantially, suggesting that a bearish move is developing. - Silver ETF holdings fell by 2.4 million ounces to 463.1 million ounces in the week to the 21st of October. iShares investors divested some of their holdings but most other funds reported gentle buying, suggesting that investors remain bullish for the longer term. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **24 October 2011** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 18 October 2011; ETF data to 21 October 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**||||**TOCOM**|**Net total**|**Price**| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |||_Futures_

- The gold-platinum premium decreased gradually from the 11th of October, falling from almost $150 per ounce to $120, suggesting that traders and investors were happy to accept a little more risk as European leaders seemed to be coming to some form of agreement on a way to tackle the Euro debt crisis. In most ways, though platinum behaved in the same way as gold in price terms throughout this period. As the Dollar weakened, also due to greater acceptance of risk, platinum climbed higher, aided by fresh buying as the Shanghai Gold Exchange started trading once again following the extended National Day holidays. As platinum reached $1,580 on the 17th, many market participants must have thought the worst was over in price terms. They we

re wrong. Weak Chinese economic data drove fresh selling and platinum dropped to $1,520 on the 18th before bouncing back over $1,550. However, selling pressure spilled over from other markets and platinum fell to $1,480 on the 20th, well below attractive prices for primary producers of the metal. A return of positive sentiment rescued platinum, though, sending it back to its current $1,535. - NYMEX platinum positions climbed by 23,000 ounces in the week to the 18th of October, although this was offset by 25,000 ounces of selling by TOCOM investors. Net long speculative NYMEX positions climbed above one million ounces as investors covered short positions, driving open interest lower. - Platinum ETF holdings declined for the sixth successive week leading up to the 21st of October, falling by 8,600 ounces. They now stand at 1.47 million ounces. There were small net inflows into the Julius Baer fund and more substantial buying for the ZKB fund. However, this was outweighed by continued outflows from the Source fund. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **24 October 2011** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 18 October 2011; ETF data to 21 October 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

Nonetheless, palladium traded as low of $580 and as high as $645. Amongst the precious metals, palladium is often the metal which gains most from returning appetite for risk. So, as the market slowly turned its thoughts to buying after the extended sell-off across a range of assets, palladium moved higher. It stumbled initially, on the 11th, as Slovakia voted against the extension of the EFSF’s role in the Euro crisis. Downgrades of the credit ratings of several European banks drove palladium to a low of $590 on the 13th before Slovakia voted again, this time extending the EFSF’s mandate. Palladium shot higher, touching $650, assisted by news reports that Russian state palladium sales might be quite limited in 2011 and 2012. The highs were short-lived, though

. As with the other metals, weak Chinese economic growth data started another round of selling and palladium eventually stopped at $580 as the US Dollar turned around and started to weaken again. Current market expectations on the Euro crisis are more positive than in recent weeks and palladium has firmed to above $625. Palladium Exchange Investment, Apr 09—October 11

• Investors trimmed their long exposure to palladium on the futures exchanges in the week to the 18th of October. However, the selling action was tiny with combined net long speculative positions on NYMEX and TOCOM falling only by 3,100 ounces to 686 million ounces. Open interest on NYMEX increased by 331 lots with both long and short positions increasing. - The selling previously seen from the palladium ETFs finally came to a halt in the week to the 21st of October as the palladium price wrestled with the psychologically important $600 level. With holdings now back to the level of mid-2010, we could see a more sustained slowdown in selling.
